hypotheses.justification:
`Wff.Holds` uses ordinary Tarski semantics (SemanticCore/Basic.lean: `.all x p` holds iff `∀ a, Wff.Holds S (update v x a) p`). The class terms `synCsn` and `synCopk` pick their bound variables with `freshVar` over the free variables, so they cannot capture anything. Suppose z = w. Then `.all z (.all z φ)` under `update v y Y` says that φ holds under `update (update (update v y Y) z Z) z W = update (update v y Y) z W` for every W. That is exactly the case Z = W of the axiom instance `hY`, which reads ⟨{Z},{W}⟩ ∈ Y ↔ ⟨Z,W⟩ ∈ v x. So the statement still holds.

The proof uses `hzw` only to prove `hz : v' z = lookup xs 1`. A uniform fix needs no case split. Take `xs := DVec.cons W (DVec.cons (v' z) (DVec.cons Y (DVec.cons (v x) DVec.nil)))` and `hiff := formulaHolds_biimp.mp (hY (v' z) W)`. Then `hz` holds by definition, `hw : v' w = W` follows from `update_same`, `hy` uses only `hyw` and `hyz`, and `hx` uses `hxw`, `hxz` and `hxy`. Finally, `holds_literalSingletonPairMem` and `holds_literalPairMem` (NFCompactLeafEndpoints.lean) only need the three equations `ha hb hr`; they assume no distinctness. The calc goes through unchanged.
